svg.title: Visual symptoms not from the eyeball: double vision sorts by which nerve palsy (third, fourth or sixth), a gaze-evoked nystagmus points to the cerebellum or brainstem, unequal pupils sort by whether the difference is worse in light (parasympathetic) or dark (sympathetic, Horner), and a relative afferent pupillary defect points to one optic nerve; nystagmus is pendular or (mostly) jerk; a missing visual field localizes along the visual pathway, to the optic nerve or chiasm (one eye, bitemporal), the optic tract and radiations (homonymous), or the occipital lobe (macular sparing, quadrantanopia, central scotomas)
